clue.text: Fruit from Thailand stored in abandoned canneries

indicators.note: stored in says the Thailand letter is kept inside the reworked cannery letters
abandoned suggests something left in disarray, so the letters of canneries are rearranged

parts.note: T is the international vehicle registration code for Thailand

explanation.surface: Imported Thai fruit is found sitting in derelict canning factories.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange CANNERIES to NECARINES and slip T in after the C.
explanation.definitionFit: A nectarine is a smooth-skinned variety of peach, so it is an example of a fruit.

clue.text: Some fasten a pendant here

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Advice on where to do up the clasp of a necklace.
explanation.definitionFit: A pendant necklace is fastened behind the neck, at the spot the clue points to with 'here'; the answer is that back part of the neck.

clue.text: Underground worker runs after dog

indicators.note: after puts the runs letter behind the dog in the answer

parts.note: a collie is a breed of sheepdog
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A miner is running behind a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A collier is a coal miner, someone who works below ground in a pit.

clue.text: Blundering on, prince acted foolishly

indicators.note: foolishly suggests things done in a muddled way, so the letters of on, prince and acted are rearranged

explanation.surface: A royal made a mess of things by behaving like a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone accident-prone is clumsy and keeps having mishaps, which is what blundering describes.

clue.text: Complete reversal of Northern Ireland diplomacy

indicators.note: reversal of says the abbreviation for Northern Ireland is read backwards

parts.note: tact is skill in handling people delicately, a synonym of diplomacy

explanation.surface: A political headline about a total U-turn in Northern Irish diplomatic policy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something intact is whole and undamaged, so it is complete.

clue.text: Microscopic part of outspoken newspaper article

indicators.note: outspoken here means said out loud, so the name of the newspaper is replaced by a word sounding the same

parts.note: the i is a British national daily newspaper; said aloud it sounds like the organ of sight
a piece is an article in a newspaper

explanation.surface: Seems to be about a frank article in a paper on microscopy.
explanation.walkthrough: The i is a UK daily paper (the sister of the Independent), so its name sounds like the lens-bearing organ.
explanation.definitionFit: The eyepiece is the lens a user looks through on a microscope, so it is one component of the instrument.

clue.text: Book initially ignored irrefutable data

indicators.note: initially ignored says the first letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: facts are pieces of information that cannot be disputed

explanation.surface: Someone writing a book chose to overlook hard evidence at first.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the F from FACTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Acts, short for the Acts of the Apostles, is a book of the New Testament.

clue.text: Secretary interrupts confab over source of imported food

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the first part sits above the next one
interrupts says the secretary letters break into the confab word

parts.note: a confab is an informal talk, a chat
PA, personal assistant, is a secretary

indicators.note: source of takes the first letter of imported

parts.note: taken from the start of this word

explanation.surface: An office assistant butts into a conversation about where some imported food came from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Food' alone is the definition; 'source of imported' is wordplay, not a hint that the food is foreign, though this Indian bread happens to be.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapati is an unleavened Indian flatbread, so it is a kind of food.

clue.text: Ship heels precariously on axis in awkward fashion

indicators.note: in a down clue on means the first part rests above the next one
precariously suggests something unstable and tipping over, so the letters of ship and heels are rearranged

parts.note: Y names an axis on a graph, the y-axis

explanation.surface: A vessel lists dangerously as it turns about its axis, an ungainly sight.
explanation.walkthrough: SHIP HEELS rearranges to SHEEPISHL, placed above Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting sheepishly means acting with embarrassment, in an awkward, self-conscious manner.

clue.text: Creature caught in meadow hiding in grass

indicators.note: hiding in says the meadow-and-caught letters are concealed within the grass word

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis, also called grass

indicators.note: in says the caught letter sits inside the meadow word

parts.note: a lea is a meadow, a poetic word
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: An animal caught in a field was hiding in the long grass.
explanation.walkthrough: Grass is not vegetation here: it is the drug, POT.
explanation.definitionFit: A polecat is a small carnivorous mammal of the weasel family, so it is a creature.

clue.text: Tennyson was oddly detached about capture

indicators.note: oddly detached says the odd-numbered letters are removed, leaving the even ones

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: The poet Tennyson was strangely aloof concerning his imprisonment.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the odd letters of TENNYSON WAS leaves ENSNA; add RE.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensnare is to catch in a trap, so it means to capture.

clue.text: Two ways around forest, one way across stream

indicators.note: around says the two street abbreviations surround the forest

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way; two of them give STST
Epping Forest is an ancient woodland on the north-east edge of London

explanation.surface: Directions: two paths circle a wood, and one route crosses a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: Epping Forest is a large ancient woodland just outside London, so 'forest' gives its name. 'One' looks like part of the definition but belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepping stone is a stone placed in water so walkers can cross dry-shod, a route over a brook.

clue.text: Very suggestive article rejected, being motivated by revenge

indicators.note: rejected says the article is thrown out of the synonym

parts.note: indicative means suggestive, pointing to something
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A racy piece of writing was turned down out of spite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very suggestive' reads as racy, but suggestive here means INDICATIVE, which loses its A.
explanation.definitionFit: Vindictive means vengeful, having a strong wish to hurt someone in return for a wrong.

clue.text: Measure of a parliamentarian

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Seems to ask how one sizes up a politician.
explanation.definitionFit: The amp, short for ampere, is the unit by which electric current is measured.

clue.text: Dishevelled teacher teased outside entrance to library

parts.note: BEd, Bachelor of Education, is a teacher's degree, standing for a teacher

indicators.note: outside says the teased word goes round the library letter

parts.note: to rag someone is to tease them, so ragged means teased

indicators.note: entrance to takes the first letter of library

parts.note: taken from the start of this word

explanation.surface: An untidy schoolteacher was mocked outside the library doors.
explanation.walkthrough: A BEd is a Bachelor of Education degree. RAGGED wraps round L to give RAGGLED.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedraggled means wet, dirty and untidy in appearance, as dishevelled does.

clue.text: Knight, say, finally quitting day job

indicators.note: finally quitting says the last letter leaves the word

parts.note: a knight errant is a wandering knight of romance, so errant can describe a knight

explanation.surface: A knight finally walks out of his day job.
explanation.walkthrough: ERRANT, the word attached to a roving knight, loses its final T.
explanation.definitionFit: An errand is a short trip to do a task, a small job.

clue.text: They question Americans in East End about Charlie

indicators.note: about says the Americans word goes round the Charlie letter

parts.note: in Cockney rhyming slang a Yank is a septic tank, shortened to septic
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Seems to describe interrogators of Americans in a London district.
explanation.walkthrough: The East End is London's traditional Cockney area; its rhyming slang turns Yanks into septic tanks, hence SEPTICS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sceptics are doubters who query claims rather than accepting them, so they are people who question.

clue.text: Leader regularly concealed rancour, supporting reinstated minister

indicators.note: in a down clue supporting means this part sits below the minister

parts.note: Michael Gove, a UK cabinet minister who was sacked and later brought back to government

indicators.note: regularly concealed says every other letter of rancour is hidden away, leaving the alternate ones

explanation.surface: A leader kept resentment under wraps while backing a minister brought back into office.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Gove is a British Conservative politician sacked from cabinet and later reinstated. Every other letter of RANCOUR leaves RNOR, which goes under GOVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A governor is the person in charge of a state, colony or institution, a ruler or head.

clue.text: Sensitive part of record buried by clergyman

indicators.note: buried by says the record letters are sunk inside the clergyman

parts.note: a rector is a parish priest
an EP, extended play, is a kind of record

explanation.surface: A vicar is laying a sensitive document to rest.
explanation.walkthrough: Record does not mean a document here: it is the music format EP.
explanation.definitionFit: A receptor is a nerve ending or cell that responds to stimuli, so it is the sensing part of an organism.

clue.text: Sticks with popular filling for teeth

indicators.note: filling says the popular word goes inside the sticks word

parts.note: canes are walking sticks
in means popular, fashionable

explanation.surface: A dentist sticks with a favourite filling material for teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Canines are the pointed eye-teeth between the incisors and premolars.

clue.text: Elvis struggling to hold note is pitiful sound

indicators.note: to hold says the shuffled name keeps the note letter inside it
struggling suggests something writhing out of shape, so the letters of Elvis are rearranged

explanation.surface: Elvis Presley strains to sustain a note and produces a feeble noise.
explanation.walkthrough: ELVIS rearranged gives SIVEL, holding N after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: A snivel is a weak, tearful whimper, a pathetic noise.

clue.text: Priam transformed into vile, heartless monster

indicators.note: into says the transformed name goes inside the outer letters of vile
heartless means the middle letters of vile are removed, leaving its ends
transformed says the letters of Priam are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: King Priam of Troy is turned into a cruel, pitiless beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' is not describing the monster: it strips the middle from 'vile', leaving only its ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A vampire is a mythical blood-drinking undead creature, a figure of horror stories.

clue.text: A run-down area welcoming closure of donkey sanctuary

indicators.note: welcoming says the slum takes in the donkey letter

parts.note: a slum is a squalid, run-down district

indicators.note: closure of takes the last letter of donkey

parts.note: taken from the end of this word

explanation.surface: A shabby neighbourhood takes in a refuge when the donkey sanctuary shuts.
explanation.definitionFit: An asylum is a place of refuge or protection, a safe haven.

clue.text: One might be discharged from German country club?

parts.note: the UN, United Nations, is a club whose members are countries

explanation.surface: Someone is expelled from a German golf or country club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discharged' looks like being expelled from the club; it is a weapon being fired. 'Country club' is the club of countries.
explanation.definitionFit: A firearm is discharged when it is fired, so this weapon is something that can be discharged.

clue.text: Poem seen as arcane incantation

indicators.note: arcane means mysterious and obscure, so the letters of poem seen as are put into a mysterious new order

explanation.surface: A poem is regarded as an obscure magic spell.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the magic password from Ali Baba that opens the robbers' cave, a spoken charm.

clue.text: Gets old leaders to acknowledge ghastly economic situation

indicators.note: leaders to takes the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Elderly politicians must admit the economy is in a dreadful state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets old leaders' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at 'old'.
explanation.definitionFit: To age is to grow older, so the verb form with s means becomes old.

clue.text: National bird perching on city light

indicators.note: perching on puts the national and bird letters after the city in an across answer

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A national emblem bird is sitting on a city streetlight.
explanation.definitionFit: A lantern is a portable lamp with a protective case, a source of illumination.

clue.text: John can essentially forgive criminal behaviour

parts.note: john is slang for a toilet, as is loo
a tin is a can

indicators.note: essentially takes the letter at the centre of forgive

parts.note: the middle letter of this word

explanation.surface: John hopes forgiving someone's crimes is possible.
explanation.walkthrough: John is not a man here: it is slang for a lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Looting is stealing goods during riots or war, a form of crime.

clue.text: Crush flipping miserable husband

indicators.note: flipping says the miserable word is turned backwards

parts.note: sad means miserable

explanation.surface: A frustrated wife squashes her flaming gloomy husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild British swear word; it signals the turnaround.
explanation.definitionFit: To dash hopes is to crush them, so dash means destroy or shatter.

clue.text: Harlots exposed by English king's heralds

indicators.note: exposed means stripped of the outer covering, so the first and last letters are removed

parts.note: strumpets are harlots, prostitutes
ER, Edwardus Rex, is an English king's title; the 's adds S

explanation.surface: Prostitutes are unmasked by a royal messenger.
explanation.walkthrough: STRUMPETS loses its outer letters to give TRUMPET; ER is the royal cipher of King Edward, and the 's supplies S.
explanation.definitionFit: Trumpeters sound fanfares to announce arrivals, so they act as heralds.
